symptom: MDL-BE06 demanded a call to BusinessEvents.StartupBusinessEvents from the after-startup microflow. It warned on correctly wired apps (the call is a Java action the walk could not see, M4) and then, once the call was removed, told the author to add back the thing that causes a DOUBLE start: both apps logged `Business events started successfully` plus the module-running-mode line twice per boot, a few milliseconds apart (ako/mxcli#2384 B1)
cause: The rule's premise was wrong. From Mendix 11.16.1, MxBuild starts the module itself: it writes a microflow `BusinessEvents.ASu_BusinessEvents` into the compiled model (deployment/model/model.mdp) that exists in neither the project nor the module package (BusinessEvents_3.12.1.mpk), and injects a call to it into the app's after-startup microflow; that generated microflow calls ConsumeBusinessEvent (which registers the consumers) and then StartupBusinessEvents. An explicit call is a second start, and HeartbeatService.init assigns a fresh ScheduledExecutorService to its static pulseThread without shutting down the pool already there, so two starts leak a pool and leave two heartbeat schedules running, of which ShutdownBusinessEvents stops only the last
file: `mdl/executor/validate_business_event_consumers.go`: businessEventsStartupWarning inverted (warns on a call, not on its absence), gated by `mxbuildWiresStartupFrom` = 11.16.1 via `ctx.Backend.ProjectVersion()`; `scriptWiresBusinessEventsStartup` became `scriptAddsBusinessEventsStartupCall`; the missing-after-startup warning dropped. Docs: the business-events skill gained "Do not start the module yourself", error-messages.md and PROPOSAL_kafka_event_integration.md §1/§5.1 corrected
insight: **The compiled model is not the project.** I checked the .mpk and the project and concluded from their silence that nothing started the module — but MxBuild GENERATES model content at build time, and `deployment/model/model.mdp` held a microflow present in neither source artefact. Reading the sources and treating their silence as proof is the error; the reporter settled it with an OpenTelemetry trace of one boot (`mxcli run --trace`) plus the compiled model, which showed one thread, two executions, one through the generated sub-microflow and one direct. For any claim about what the platform does at runtime, the compiled model and a trace outrank the project and the module package. Second lesson, from the controls: stubbing the version gate to `return true` / `return false` left `pv` unused, so both stubs were COMPILE failures that my grep read as passes — a control must be shown to compile and run, not merely to produce no FAIL line. Moving the gate constant instead (10.0.0 and 99.0.0) failed exactly the intended cases. The gate sits at the one version measured: below it the call is required, and warning against it would mirror the defect being fixed. Nothing is asserted about a missing after-startup microflow, because whether MxBuild supplies one is unmeasured — the same kind of assumption that caused this.
